correctness.rationale: In a fixed real n-dimensional ℓ_p central hyperplane, the polar section formula V_{n,p}(a)=1/(n−1)∫_{S(a⊥)}(Σ|u_i|^p)^(-(n−1)/p) dσ is valid even n=2. Uniform in normal a, differentiation at p=2 yields derivative G(a)=−1/4 Σ_i q_i log q_i−(n−1)c_{n−1}/2, with q_i=1−a_i² and c_m=(ψ(3/2)−ψ((m+2)/2))/2. Strong convexity of h(x)=x log x for x≤1, with Σ_i q_i=n−1, gives G(d)−G(a)≥D(a)/8, D=Σ(a_i²−1/n)². The spherical Hessian at each signed diagonal is −∥v∥²/(n−1); locally the ratio [G(d)−G(a)]/D→n/[8(n−1)]. C² convergence of the normalized first p variation near those finitely many signed-diagonal normals supplies a uniform local lower bound D/16 for p−2>0 small; uniform first variation and compactness away from this orbit supply the global bound. Therefore V_{n,p}(d)−V_{n,p}(a)≥κ_{n−1}(p−2)D/16 for all unit a and 2<p<2+δ_n, δ_n depending on n. Assumptions n fixed, real ℓ_p and intrinsic Euclidean sections are essential. Quadrature is only a spot check of the exact proof.

value.rationale: This supplies a structurally nontrivial fixed-dimensional resolution of the diagonal-maximizer question in a near-Euclidean superquadratic region, together with a uniform directional quadratic stability deficit—not merely a derivative sign at one normal or an asymptotic dimension-free comparison. The diagonal normal is a canonical section candidate, and fixed n and p↓2 are natural boundary regimes. The theorem explicitly disclaims a quantitative dimension-independent δ_n.

limitations: Uniform C² convergence needs nonzero coordinate coefficients near each signed diagonal; the proof supplies this and controls integrated logarithms.
No all-p interval or dimension-independent δ_n established.
